_comment: Coverage ledger for the SL-ABI-V3 §5 tape transplant, gated by
notCarried: a wizard wz_deck_* entry point deliberately NOT carried into
sl_tape_*, with the reason. Empty is the good state — it means the
additions: an sl_tape_* entry point with no wizard counterpart, with the
reason it exists. Both lists are required so neither a dropped function
nor an invented one can pass unnoticed.

additions.name: sl_tape_count
additions.reason: Tapes and grid decks are separate index spaces in the merged engine, so a caller needs to ask how many tapes exist. Wizard had one deck array and a compile-time constant, and no equivalent getter.

additions.name: sl_tape_channels
additions.reason: The drain ring is interleaved at the tape's own width, so the host must know it to size a drain buffer and to open the take's WAV. Wizard's host knew the width implicitly because it chose the record channels itself; with a mainMix source the engine picks the width, so it has to be readable.

additions.name: sl_tape_state
additions.reason: Wizard published deck state through its HotFrame deck block, which v3 does not have yet (per-deck HotFrame fields are still zero-filled). Until it does, state has to be readable directly or the UI cannot tell recording from looping.

additions.name: sl_tape_record_cap_reached
additions.reason: Same as sl_tape_state — wizard surfaced the 256 MB cap flag via its HotFrame deck block. A cap that stops a recording with no way to observe it is the silent-truncation failure D-WZ-DECK-01 exists to make visible.

additions.name: sl_tape_set_tempo_mode
additions.reason: P3-2b-5 (TAPE-STRETCH.md): 0 timePitch / 1 timeStretch — what the one rate number DRIVES. Wizard's deck had varispeed only; pitch-preserving stretch is the merge's 'stretch and re-pitch every element to the master' made real for tapes, on scoopy's own Signalsmith stretcher.

additions.name: sl_tape_tempo_mode
additions.reason: The readback for sl_tape_set_tempo_mode, so the dispatcher and fixtures can verify what landed rather than trusting the send (the silent-refusal defect class params:check exists for).

additions.name: sl_tape_stretch_ready
additions.reason: The stretcher warms up ASYNC (~600 ms) and the render stays dry until it is warm; without an introspection point the fixture could only sleep-and-hope, and a UI lamp could never say why stretch has not engaged yet.

additions.name: sl_tape_scrub_rate
additions.reason: The readback for pubScrubRate, which the render has published since the transplant and NOTHING could read — no getter, no HotFrame slot, no reader anywhere (scratching.md §4.5 records it as a trap). Wizard had no equivalent because its deck published rate through the HotFrame deck block that v3 does not have yet, the same gap sl_tape_state and sl_tape_record_cap_reached exist to cover. A rate the engine publishes and nobody can read is telemetry that only looks like telemetry.

additions.name: sl_tape_scratch_start
additions.reason: Turntablism scratch (docs/specs/scratching.md): a tempo-locked gesture that runs while held, driving the SAME scrub path a finger does. Wizard's deck had no auto-gesture of any kind. It is in the ENGINE rather than a host block callback because processBlock exists only in the plugins — the app renders through SlRenderSink's four-line adapter with no per-block hook — and because per-sample evaluation removes the ~94 Hz control-rate ceiling that smeared each reversal across a block. Takes an sl_scratch_params STRUCT rather than positional doubles: five [0,1]-ish parameters in a row is a silent-miscall waiting to happen, and the fields name themselves at every call site.

additions.name: sl_tape_scratch_set
additions.reason: Retune period, span, cut, vary and spread while the gesture is HELD, without re-seeding the phase — a period change mid-stroke must change speed, not restart the figure. Separate from scratch_start for exactly that reason: reusing start would make every knob movement a restart, which is audible and wrong.

additions.name: sl_tape_scratch_stop
additions.reason: Release, which COMPLETES THE CURRENT STROKE before letting go: reversals land at the extrema and strokes are whole units, so cutting mid-stroke hands the scrub coast a playhead the gesture never rests at, and from there the region `entry` snap is a jump nobody asked for. Distinct from sl_tape_scrub_end, which releases immediately because a finger genuinely has let go.

additions.name: sl_tape_set_scratch_tempo
additions.reason: The tempo scratch patterns lock to. The engine has no tempo of its own to read — its only tempo concept is a per-deck sync RATIO (sl_deck_set_tempo_sync) — so whoever knows must push it: ScoopyTape from HostSync inside processBlock, Studio from the master tempo. Engine-wide rather than per-tape because a pattern is locked to THE tempo, and eight tapes disagreeing about the length of a 1/8 note would be eight clocks. Wizard's deck had no tempo input at all.

additions.name: sl_tape_scratch_fader
additions.reason: The PLAYER's own hand on the crossfader during a scratch, 0 shut .. 1 open, resting open. Multiplies the technique's gate rather than replacing it — the pattern is a figure the fader hand plays, and this is the hand on top of it, which is what lets you cut a pattern that is itself chopping. Shaped by the measured BATTLE CURVE (a 45 mm run whose silence-to-full transition spans 2-3 mm) rather than linearly, because the dead ground either side is where the hand rests and is what makes clicking fast possible at all. Wizard had no crossfader anywhere.
